children: is leveraging its captive audience and extensive digital menu board network to display ads for third-party brands, creating a new source of high-margin revenue.

The hamburger chain, which serves as many as 26 million Americans a day, is testing the initiative at select company-owned restaurants, turning customers’ wait time into an opportunity to “entertain” them with digital ads for relevant products and services.

“This limited menu board advertising pilot at select company-owned restaurants is exploring ways to share post-purchase content that customers may find helpful, relevant, or interesting, while ensuring the McDonald’s experience remains at the center of every visit,” a McDonald’s spokesperson said in an email to Bloomberg.
The ads will be placed on digital boards at drive-thrus and in restaurant touch-screen kiosks.
